✦ Your Guides at the Signpost

Built by Brother & Sister Architects

“Pull up a chair by the lantern! Over at Ocean View Archives, our friends Isabel, Eleanor, Sophia, and Oliver guard the great single-timeline novels. Out here on the porch, my brother Rowan and I build the signposts for stories meant to branch—where every single trail you pick leads somewhere whole, honest, and worth the walk.”

Rowan maps the diverging trails so every option leads to a true horizon, while Iris stamps the 2-Way and 3-Way Compass Medallions and keeps every route’s memory intact.

The Story Crossroads Promise

Why Rowan and Iris built a dedicated home alongside Ocean View Archives specifically for branching novels.

🧭

Every Route Is Coequal

Rowan’s first rule at the drafting desk: there are never abrupt dead ends or "wrong answers." Every option opens a complete, thoughtfully written storyline.

📖

Novel-Grade Literary Prose

Each Story Crossroads edition reads with the same rich sensory atmosphere, emotional warmth, and lived-in dialogue as our Ocean View Archives novels.

🌲

Self-Contained Worlds

Purpose-built standalone settings give your choices genuine room to reshape where characters live, what they build, and who they become.

🔖

Step Back Anytime

Iris’s route-memory ribbon remembers your active path across chapters while letting you return to any Crossroads signpost with a single tap.

🧭 Guided by Rowan & Iris

Step Up to the Signpost

Rowan set three lanterns out on the evening trail so you can feel how a Story Crossroads works in real time—pick a 3-Way trail, follow it into a 2-Way Crossroads, and use Iris’s trail pills to step back anytime.

🌲 Inaugural 3-Way Edition

Featured Edition: Cedar Run

3-Way Story Crossroads Edition • Summer 2000 • Northeast Washington Wilderness

Cedar Run — Book One: First Foothold in the Valley

Turned out on the evening of their eighteenth birthday simply for refusing to scatter onto three separate lives, fraternal brother Luke and identical twin sisters Tessa and Sadie Bridger step past their backyard fence into deep old-growth cedar forest with Grandpa Owen Sawyer’s canvas tool roll and 1974 mahogany guitar.

Rowan & Iris’s Field Note: “Luke, Tessa, and Sadie Bridger refused to let anyone split the three of them apart at eighteen. At their first Crossroads, you help all three triplets choose where in the valley to build their shelter together.”

  • Option 1 • Creek-Side Timber The Creek-Bend Cedar Bench

    Split straight-grained windfall western red cedar planks beside cutthroat trout pools and soothing mountain rain.

  • Option 2 • Dry-Stone Hearth The Granite Overhang

    Dry-stack warm Kettle Range granite beneath a natural rock ceiling thirty feet above the valley floor.

  • Option 3 • High Meadow Spring The Forgotten Stone Springhouse

    Restore an overgrown 1930s mossy stone springhouse beside cold artesian water and wild huckleberry slopes.

3-Way Story Crossroads Edition • 1980s Fantasy Realm of Vaeloria • Twin Moons

The Uncharted Waystation — Book One: Beyond the Studio Rift

Twenty-four-year-old Nolan Lennox and his tall nineteen-year-old sister Gwen tumble barefoot in jeans and cotton t-shirts off their shared full-sized studio bed into the distant twin-moon borderlands of Vaeloria with Grandpa Walter’s plaid blanket and four ergonomic Lofstrand forearm crutches—choosing at every Story Crossroads which gentle 1980s-fantasy road carries them inward to earn the Uncharted Waystation.

Rowan & Iris’s Field Note: “Three weeks before Gwen turned eighteen, fellow travelers at the Norfolk bus station helped push Nolan’s abusive ex away when twenty-three-year-old Nolan (5'7") refused a one-way cross-country ticket so he could go home to Chesapeake for his kid sister’s birthday. Days later, when Grandpa Walter died, Nolan rushed six-foot-one Gwen into his tiny one-person studio box—and Gwen never left his side. A year later, dropped barefoot in Vaeloria’s borderlands on forearm crutches, they must journey together, camp curled up under Grandpa’s blanket, and heal The Great Drift to earn their glowing-archway home.”

  • Option 1 • Waterway Lanterns The Glasswater Lantern-Barge Canal

    Rest bare feet on cushioned cedar planks aboard Maren’s glowing sapphire-lantern barge while navigating by double moonlight.

  • Option 2 • Cushion-Moss & Springs The Whisperwood Cushion-Moss Road

    Walk unhurriedly over three-inch-deep velvet moss built by the Slow-Footed Order beside warm 98-degree crystal mineral foot-basins.

  • Option 3 • Sky-Cable Gondolas The Brass Counterweight Gondola Way

    Glide effortlessly up the Amber Crags inside water-balanced oak-and-brass sky gondolas past singing cliffside wind-harps.
